checks.finding: Exact script and launch descriptors match submitted candidate.
Early recovery receipt confirms saved byte readback before readiness work.
All three SHA-256/size/mode tuples equal the frozen inspector constants.
Static AST and full source inspection show only six declared standard-library imports, no project/package import and no subprocess/target invocation.
The selected current interpreter uses -I -S -B and exactly the adopted five-variable clean environment.
Canonical current sys.executable is compared with /proc/self/exe, rejecting deleted/name ambiguity and binding opened device/inode to the running image.
Each image uses a no-follow read descriptor, regular-file and 64-MiB limits, stable fstat/read/fstat/named-path identity and exact byte count.
SHA-256, byte count and exact mode are compared; a failed Python pin stops before maps or other image reads.
Only after Python match, /proc/self/maps is read with a one-MiB ceiling plus one-byte overflow detection.
Libc and loader candidates are deduplicated by device/inode/path; missing, multiple, deleted or nonabsolute selected-role rows refuse.
Mapped device/inode is compared with the opened actual file; libc mismatch stops before loader file inspection.
Inner twenty-second checks and outer thirty-second timeout bound the observation; no automatic retry is selected.
All target-start and H0-acceptance claims remain false; a three-pin match is explicitly only necessary eligibility.
Output paths are current-session paths and absent at review; the Director commits to exclusive stdout/stderr capture and prelaunch candidate rehash.
Ordinary mismatch/error records observations and exits two; a complete three-pin match exits zero without invoking H0.
Expected checker launches means one readiness Python process; the original CPU checker denominator remains zero.

allowance: Exactly one execution of this candidate through the described exclusive outer capture; the readiness harness performs data reads only.
outer_capture_obligations: Rehash exact script and launch immediately before execution.
Use the exact argv/cwd/environment and outer timeout.
Create stdout and stderr exclusively; preserve them and a structured launch result even on failure/timeout.
No retry after first failure, unknown result or timeout; preserve exact outcome and stop technical work for review.
observation_scope: Current process executable pathname and kernel device/inode relationship.
Stable on-disk bytes/mode of selected Python, then selected mapped libc and loader if prior pins pass.
A single bounded proc maps snapshot; not proof that every mapped byte or the entire operating system is authenticated.
not_accepted: Actual current installation receipts or package metadata

reviewer_execution.method: Full source/launch read plus data-only AST, descriptors and output absence checks.

next_action: Director runs the accepted readiness candidate once and returns exact outer outcome/stdout/stderr for independent review. Stop on its first concrete mismatch or ambiguity.
